A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GMM-GDA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph-classification accuracies, structural-corruption experiments, influence analyses, configuration-model and density-fitting ablations, and training timings.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds density-estimation comparisons involving KDE, copulas, GANs, and variational Bayesian fitting on GIN representations.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure: train the GNN, fit class-specific GMMs to graph embeddings, sample representations, and fine-tune the post-readout classifier. Alternative density estimators are evaluated as comparators, without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate graph classification on IMDB-BINARY, IMDB-MULTI, MUTAG, PROTEINS, and DD, retaining the same training-edge corruption scenarios. The added density-estimation comparisons reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds KDE, copula, and GAN comparators, with the GAN described as tGAN, to the previous EM-versus-VB comparison. Tables 5–6 evaluate these alternatives on both backbones, substantially broadening comparisons of the central density-model choice. The main graph-augmentation comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The density-estimation ablation expands from the GCN results in v1 Table 5 to separate GCN and GIN evaluations in v2 Tables 5–6. The stated main splits, two-layer 32-dimensional backbones, training budgets, accuracy metric, and corruption settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D expands from comparing two ways to fit a GMM into testing whether alternative distribution families can replace GMMs, across both backbones. This substantially strengthens examination of a central design choice. Configuration-model, structural-corruption, and influence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy with standard deviations and mean timings. V2 continues the same reporting practice for added results, without introducing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add substantial comparative results for KDE, copulas, and GANs across five datasets and both backbones, plus GIN-VBI results. For example, GAN ties GMM-EM's GIN mean accuracy at 88.83% on MUTAG and 71.33% on PROTEINS. Earlier benchmark, corruption, configuration-model, and timing values remain unchanged; the GIN-EM row repeats existing Table 2 results.

T1.justification: V2 distinguishes the expected-augmentation empirical minimizer from its finite-sampling approximation and revises Appendix A's bounded-difference derivation. Section 3.1 adds a bounded-node-count assumption and norm-equivalence argument; new Appendix G defines structural, combined structure-feature, and permutation-adjusted graph distances. The principal theorem bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about the generalization framework, efficient GMM-based augmentation, influence-function analysis, and robustness. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the added ablations as supporting GMM density modeling and discusses competitive GAN accuracy with additional training costs. Appendix E adds an augmentation-reuse explanation and incorrectly claims that only GeoMix is faster: Table 7 also shows faster G-Mixup training, including 148.71 versus 774.47 seconds on IMDB-BINARY.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E add high-level fitting and sampling descriptions for new comparators and explicitly state that generated representations are reused across epochs. Original hardware, hyperparameters, Gaussian-component counts, and the code link are retained. Detailed settings for the new density estimators are not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds Härdle et al. (2004) for KDE and Nelsen (2006) for copulas. It removes Bishop and Nasrabadi (2006), using the already-cited Tzikas et al. (2008) for variational Bayesian estimation. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized: Appendix D becomes an expanded, itemized explanation, Appendix E gains discussion, Appendix G is added, and Section 3.1 receives clarification. An author affiliation and some notation are corrected. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 5 expands to five density-estimation methods with a clearer GCN caption, and a separate GIN Table 6 is added with result highlighting. Subsequent tables are renumbered and repaginated. Figures 1–2 and the main experimental table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's EM-versus-VB study, v2 provides more informative tests of the density-model choice and clarifies the estimator, graph distances, and proof reasoning. These yield a modest net improvement. The gains are limited by sparse settings for the new comparators and Appendix E's erroneous timing interpretation, which conflicts with the retained G-Mixup measurements in Table 7.
